section_1.title: Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows
section_1.content: Briefly define a vector as a directed line segment with magnitude and direction. Introduce scalar multiplication and vector addition as the building blocks of the space.
section_1.example: Visualizing a 2D plane: A vector v=(2,1) moves 2 steps East and 1 step North.

section_2.title: Linear Combinations and Span
section_2.content: Explain that a linear combination is a sum of vectors scaled by constants. The 'Span' is the set of all possible points reachable by combining these vectors. Use a graphical animation of a plane filling up.
section_2.example: Two robots moving on a 2D floor: Robot A moves along vector u, Robot B along vector v. Their combined positions span the entire 2D floor.

section_3.title: Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule
section_3.content: Define linear dependence as a situation where one vector can be written as a combination of others. Visually, these vectors lie on the same line or plane. If they are 'dependent,' they don't add new directions to the span.
section_3.example: Three characters walking in a line: If Person C is just walking along the path already covered by Person A and B, Person C is 'redundant'—the set is linearly dependent.

section_4.title: Bases: The Minimalist Toolkit
section_4.content: Introduce a 'Basis' as the most efficient set of vectors that span a space without redundancy. A basis must be linearly independent and span the entire space.
section_4.example: The standard unit vectors (1,0) and (0,1) acting as the GPS grid of a map—they provide the simplest way to reach any location in the coordinate system.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Review: Span (Reach), Independence (Efficiency), and Basis (The perfect set). Connect these concepts to high-dimensional data processing.
section_5.example: A 3D video game engine: Uses a basis of 3 vectors to define every object's position in 3D space.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.5 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations and Span", [
            "Linear combination sums scaled vectors.",
            "The Span is the reach of all combinations.",
            "Two vectors span a 2D floor.",
            "Robot movements combine to cover the floor.",
            "Span reveals all reachable space points."
        ])

        # Define axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes)

        # Vectors
        v = Arrow(ORIGIN, axes.c2p(2, 1), color="#33FF57", buff=0)
        w = Arrow(ORIGIN, axes.c2p(-1, 2), color="#3357FF", buff=0)
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#33FF57").next_to(v.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        w_label = MathTex(r"\vec{w}", color="#3357FF").next_to(w.get_end(), LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # Span area
        span_area = Polygon(
            axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(2, 1), axes.c2p(1, 3), axes.c2p(-1, 2),
            fill_opacity=0.3, fill_color="#808080", stroke_width=0
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#3357FF")
        self.play(Create(w), Write(w_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(span_area))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Represent combination movement
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        dot.move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1.5)), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Indicate(span_area))
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.",
            "Add two vectors: tip to tail.",
            "Scale vectors: stretching or shrinking length.",
            "Vector v (2,1) moves East 2, North 1.",
            "Vectors are building blocks of linear space."

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a vector Arrow from origin to (2, 2) in #FF5733 color.

        v_label = Text("v", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # Group and position

        v_label.next_to(v_vector.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(v_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
